plainProblem: Edit Distance: Picture the puzzle 'Edit Distance'. Worked example — input: word1 = "horse", word2 = "ros"; expected output: 3. Why: 3 edits. Interview pattern to name out loud: 2-D dynamic programming.

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Edit Distance”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input word1 = "horse", word2 = "ros" should still produce 3.

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: See code.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: The key idea is to use dynamic programming to calculate the minimum number of operations (insert, delete, or replace) required to transform one string 'word1' into another string 'word2'. We can define a 2D table 'dp' where dp[i][j] represents the minimum edit distance between the first 'i' characters of 'word1' and the first 'j' characters of 'word2'.
